title: An integrator asked to stop drains instead of killing: it starts no gate, lets running gates record and land within a bound, then exits 0; a deploy no longer costs a running gate
prompt:
Read, in crates/spawn-cli/src/integrate.rs, the module comment ("Gates run per mission, on threads"), how a gate thread starts and records, and what happens to running gates when the process gets TERM; crates/spawn-cli/src/integrate/warm.rs (why nothing the integrator starts may outlive it unaccounted: parent-death signal, process group, cgroup, pid file): keep that guarantee; deploy/deploy.sh and deploy/systemd/spawn-integrate.service (you may not edit them: how the owner restarts the integrator); rsi/backlog/021.json and 034.json (owner pushes and holds: a hold keeps landings off a source while gates still run).

The problem. Restarting the integrator kills every running gate, which then starts again from nothing: on 2026-11-09 at 10:33 a deploy restarted it 22 minutes into task 210's gate (which then took 70 minutes in all); objective 021 measured task 48 losing a 40-minute gate to a stop. Gates run 17 minutes on average and up to 101. Letting a gate outlive the integrator would break warm.rs's guarantee, so the integrator must finish what it started before it goes.

Required behaviour. A drain request (SIGUSR1 to the integrator, or `spawn integrate --drain` with the same --root, which sends it to the integrator running there, waits until that process is gone and exits 0) makes the integrator record `integrator.draining` {`gates`: the tasks whose gates run, as numbers, `bound_s`}, start no gate and no base warm (nor any other background judging) from then on, and keep its passes going otherwise (records, holds, assignment, the landing of a verdict that arrives). Once no gate of its runs and the verdicts they recorded were acted on (an accepted task landed), it records `integrator.drained` and exits 0. SPAWN_INTEGRATE_DRAIN_SECS (counted from the `integrator.draining` record; default 7200; a whole number from 1 to 86400, any other value refused at start: the integrator exits non-zero naming it and judges nothing) bounds the drain: at the bound the integrator stops the gates still running (their process groups, as a gate past its time limit is stopped: nothing of theirs outlives it), records nothing for them, records `integrator.drain_expired` {`gates`: those tasks, `bound_s`} and exits 0. The dispatcher's digest tells the supervisor of an expired drain once (session `host`, tag `host integrator-drain-expired-<event id>`, its line naming each task as `task #<id>`). TERM keeps today's behaviour: the process stops at once and records no drain. The store accepts the three `integrator.*` records from the integrator (crates/spawn-postgres/sql/schema.sql, `spawn_integrator_record`).

The gate judges this with rsi/scenarios/037.sh (read its header): a real loop with two residents on two sources and a real integrator judging through a recording gate whose runs are held; a drain request while task A's gate runs: `integrator.draining` names [A] with bound 7200 while `--drain` waits; task B, reported meanwhile, gets no gate; released, A is accepted and lands, then `integrator.drained`, exit 0, `--drain` exits 0, and no base warm ran for the landing; four invalid SPAWN_INTEGRATE_DRAIN_SECS values are refused at start; with a 3 s bound and SIGUSR1, `integrator.drain_expired` names [B] at or after the bound, the integrator exits 0, B's gate process is gone within 5 s and B has no verdict; the supervisor is told of that expiry once; TERM still stops at once with no drain record. It fails at (1) on the live main (984d059): `spawn integrate --drain` is refused by the usage.

What it saves. The owner's deploy drains (deploy.sh change, owner side) and loses no gate: 22-40 minutes per deploy measured, more on a busy host. Throughput and lead time improve; no verdict changes.

Rules: never edit the protected paths, which the gate rejects: rsi/, scripts/ (scripts/rsi/, scripts/blackbox/, scripts/e2e.sh among them), deploy/, all of web/ except web/src/ and web/index.html, rust-toolchain files and .cargo/. The gate also rejects fewer runnable tests than the base, any lint relaxation and any build-time code. The gate builds offline from the cargo caches already on the host. Keep every existing check green and add tests of your own for the new behaviour.
